name: manual_f7c090
claim: When supervising child processes via HTTP loopback proxies under spend bounds, enforce four structural patterns: (1) Synchronous socket admission in process_request before spawning handler threads to eliminate accept-to-dispatch races against early child exits; (2) Two-phase stop_and_drain shutdown setting _accepting=False, calling server.shutdown(), and awaiting condition variable drain; (3) Single fail-closed funnel in _fail_closed and _read_upstream_response ensuring all transport/read errors (including HTTPError.read timeouts) terminate fail-closed with exit 124; (4) Pre-forward provider-side budget clamping of max_tokens and max_completion_tokens to prevent runaway token spend before upstream generation occurs. On distributed task queues, preserve monotonic claim timestamps (float) as fencing tokens rather than degrading to boolean or None.

decisions.notes: Enduring architectural lessons distilled from CodeRabbitAi and Perplexity remediation cycles on diazMelgarejo/orama-system PR #533 and Perpetua-Tools PR #525. Codifies four structural loopback proxy invariants for child process supervision and distributed fencing preservation.
